nodes.label: The competition regime reaches asymmetric growth, NOT true competitive exclus...
nodes.statement: The competition regime reaches asymmetric growth, NOT true competitive exclusion, over the run measured. The loser's biomass GREW from its 1.25 seed to 64.5 (~51.6x) -- far above the viable-biomass floor -- while shrinking to an 81-px fragment against the winner's 3511 px: it is spatially DISPLACED, not driven below any viability bound. This study couples STATE (one shared field) but imposes no viability CONSTRAINT (no death, no viability bound), exactly the paper's §Cell–cell coupling distinction that "what is coupled is not only state, but constraint" -- here, only state. The winner's 3511-px endpoint is ~97.5% of the 3600-px lattice with the field nearly exhausted by t=20, so the endpoint is partly a finite-size lattice-saturation artifact; by t≈30 the winner fills the lattice and the still-viable loser is crowded off it (eviction, not starvation).

nodes.statement: Over the same coupling process, a different composite -- a localized glucose depot, a fast-diffusing acetate byproduct, and an acetate-consuming cell role -- sustains a cell that never touches glucose purely via a spatial metabolic handoff: the consumer's local glucose reads 0.0 the entire run while its biomass still climbs, entirely on diffused acetate. This is the paper's §Cell–cell coupling relational-molecule claim made concrete -- the same acetate is the secretor's metabolic waste and the consumer's sole carbon food, its meaning set by each cell's interface (microbial cross-feeding, morris2013). Confirmed: consumer local_glucose 0.0, local_acetate 1.30, biomass 1.25 -> 3.79, ending as a viable 65-pixel CPM cell.

This closes the handoff-necessity argument the flagship left resting only on local_glucose == 0.0 + observed growth: the consumer's growth is genuinely caused by the secretor's acetate, not by anything intrinsic to the consumer or the field.

nodes.label: The cell's shed material does not vanish -- it becomes physical debris. As th...
nodes.statement:
The cell's shed material does not vanish -- it becomes physical debris. As the
domain resorbs, its vacated footprint pixels are converted into particles in a shared
map[particle] store, and that debris cloud keeps scattering (RMS spread strictly increasing)
well after the cell itself has fully dissolved, under a separate stock BrownianMovement
process. Confirmed: 68 particles shed by tick 16 (deterministic, reproduces exactly); RMS
spread ~5.3 -> ~7.6 over an 8-tick post-dissolution window in a representative run --
BrownianMovement is unseeded, so the exact magnitudes vary run-to-run, but the strict increase
is the robust, test-asserted claim.

nodes.label: Sibling cells coupled through the shared glucose field grow at different loca...
nodes.statement: Sibling cells coupled through the shared glucose field grow at different local rates as the colony crowds -- a cell on the fed rim out-competes one boxed into a depleting interior -- so division timing desynchronizes rather than staying locked to clean powers of two. This is exactly the paper's own description of what happens right after division: "these systems remain coupled through shared environmental state, so their interfaces are not independent ... enabling both coordination and divergence" (§Growth and division). It is the first emergent multicellular heterogeneity this investigation demonstrates, not a nuisance the staircase merely survives. Confirmed: the n_cells staircase departs from powers of two from tick 21 onward (5, then 11, 14, 18), and by the final sampled tick, live cells span all 5 generations (0 through 4) simultaneously in the same 18-cell colony.

nodes.label: Honesty point, load-bearing for the paper's central question. The condensate ...
nodes.statement: Honesty point, load-bearing for the paper's central question. The condensate study demonstrates a boundary forming -- phase separation, mass-conserved, with an emergent interface -- but NOT the condensate doing interface work: it does not selectively concentrate or exclude a second species. That selective-permeability property is exactly what would make the interface a functional, regulatable boundary rather than a transient or unregulated aggregate, which is the discriminator the paper's §Molecular compositions question (Fig 8) turns on. It is named here as the natural next step, not claimed as already shown. Likewise the sorting study demonstrates differential-adhesion demixing with a cohesion guard, not a molecular binding-affinity/selectivity term.

The demixing is caused by the differential-J regime, not by CPM dynamics per ...
nodes.statement: The demixing is caused by the differential-J regime, not by CPM dynamics per se. Under neutral contact energies (all J=8) the same checkerboard at T=10 stays mixed, isolating the complementarity-encoding contact-energy asymmetry as the cause of sorting. Confirmed by a neutral-J composite re-run (documented, not a committed test): neutral J holds hetero_frac ~0.52 over 600 MCS vs ~0.06 for the differential-J regime.
